summary: C1: docs/PROMISES.md maps every strong public claim (local data safety, token/cost coverage, cross-surface totals, receipts, yield, replay, performance, audit, distribution/provenance, allocations) to exact wording, behavior, a reproducible evidence command or artifact, the revision, coverage limits, and a verified/partial/unverified outcome, and links all five prerequisite remediation results plus their signed audits. The README provenance claim is now explicitly workflow-defined and unverified against a downloaded artifact, and the performance claim points to published evidence; project.jsonc wording is aligned with refreshed lastEdit. C2: the simulated user gate adds three named semantic suites (receipt/replay/audit) with minimum test-count tripwires so a renamed or missing test cannot silently pass, runs them in a neutral environment isolated from fixture tool-root overrides, and keeps all 107 existing checks (now 110 total). CLM-203 was proven with an injected failing expectation in an isolated copy (gate exit 1, 109/110), restored, and rerun green (exit 0, 110/110).

cases.evidence: docs/PROMISES.md covers every strong README/metadata promise with location, behavior, evidence, revision, limits and outcome; all 12 relative links resolve to existing files (prerequisite remediation-result.json and audit-receipt.json files included). project.jsonc feature/architecture wording now matches qualified claims (receipt sources named, delta caching without blanket sub-10ms wording, PERFORMANCE.md pointer) and lastEdit is refreshed to 26-10-15-15-11. Reviewer comparison of wording to behavior is the human sign-off step; the audit receipt records the independent review.
